analysis.title: US EQUITIES COLOR: ON THE WEEK 23 Oct 2026
key_insights: GS floor saw about $20bn of net TMT selling (Info Tech + Comm Services) over the past 2 weeks across all client types and execution channels, approaching the -$23bn net sold over 2 weeks in the July AI selling episode.
Long-only and hedge fund clients finished moderate net sellers on the week, with supply most acute in tech. Mood is described as terrible, with performance challenges persisting.

There were no signs of offense being played around the AI theme on the GS desk during the week. Last week's episode saw rotation out of AI into defensives, but there was little of that on Friday despite gains in Consumer, Utilities and pockets of Financials.
US equities were net sold for a 3rd straight week (4 of the last 5), driven mainly by long and short sales in Single Stocks, which saw the largest de-grossing since late July.

Industrials was among the most net sold sectors, with hedge funds selling the group at the fastest pace in 6+ months. Real Estate and Staples were by far the most net bought sectors, pointing to a defensive posture.
Next week is busy for macro and micro: FOMC and BOC on Wednesday, ECB on Thursday, BOJ on Friday, plus the heaviest week of Q3 earnings (44% of S&P market cap reports).
The S&P implied move through next Friday (10/30) is 1.80%.
Brazil election results are due Sunday night. Polymarket has Bolsonaro at a 76% chance of winning, while local polls show him in a slimmer 0-2.5pt lead.
